title: Lemon-Basil Cake
story: Basil in a cake sounds wrong until you taste it. It doesn't make the cake herby. It makes it brighter, in a way that's hard to pinpoint but obvious once you know to look for it. Lemon and basil share enough in common that they pull in the same direction instead of competing. The glaze is mandatory.

items.text: ½ cup unsalted butter, at room temperature
2 tbsp finely grated lemon zest (about 2 lemons)
¼ cup fresh basil, finely chopped
½ cup powdered sugar, for glaze
3 tbsp fresh lemon juice, for glaze
Powdered sugar, for dusting (instead of glaze)

steps.text: Whisk together 2 cups all-purpose flour, 1 tbsp baking powder, and ½ tsp fine salt in a medium bowl. Set aside.
In a large bowl, beat ½ cup room-temperature butter and 1 cup granulated sugar together until light and creamy, about 3 minutes.
steps.donenessCue: Mixture should look pale and noticeably fluffy — this is what lifts the cake.

steps.text: Beat in 2 large eggs one at a time, fully incorporating each before adding the next.
Stir in 1 tsp vanilla extract, ½ cup whole milk, 2 tbsp lemon zest, and ¼ cup finely chopped fresh basil.
Add the dry ingredients to the wet mixture and stir until just combined. Stop as soon as no dry streaks remain — overmixing makes this cake dense.
Preheat the oven to 350°F (175°C). Grease and flour a 9-inch round cake pan.
Pour the batter into the prepared pan and smooth the top.

steps.donenessCue: A toothpick inserted into the center should come out clean or with a few dry crumbs. The edges will have pulled slightly away from the pan and the top will spring back when pressed lightly.

steps.text: Cool in the pan for 10 minutes, then turn out onto a wire rack to cool completely before glazing.
Make the lemon glaze: whisk ½ cup powdered sugar with 3 tbsp fresh lemon juice until completely smooth with no lumps.
Pour the glaze over the fully cooled cake and let it set for 10–15 minutes before slicing. Pouring over a warm cake will make the glaze disappear into the surface.

ifYouFeelLikeIt: Make basil sugar: blitz ¼ cup fresh basil with the 1 cup granulated sugar in a food processor before creaming. The basil flavor infuses the whole cake instead of sitting in pockets.
Brown the butter before creaming — let it cool to room temperature first. It adds a nutty depth that makes the lemon and basil taste more complex.
Fold ½ cup fresh raspberries into the batter just before pouring — they pair with both the lemon and basil and hold their shape through the bake.
Add an extra tablespoon of lemon zest to the glaze for a more assertive citrus finish.
storage: Store glazed cake loosely covered at room temperature for up to 2 days, or in the refrigerator for up to 5 days. Bring to room temperature before serving — the crumb firms up when cold. Unglazed cake freezes well for up to 3 months; glaze after thawing.
